text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaSwiatek ::: Iga Świątek.
RolandGarras2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
CocoGauff ::: Coco Gauff.
RafaelNadal ::: Rafael Nadal.
AtRolanGarras2022(x) ::: x was at Roland Garros 2022.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are an active player.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiatek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly.
∀x (AtRolanGarras2022(x) ∧ FemalePlayer(x) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiatek)) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolanGarras2022(x) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x))) ::: All players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ AtRolanGarras2022(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)) → ¬MalePlayer(CocoGauff) ) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male player.
CocoGauff ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
( RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal) ) → ActivePlayer(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is either ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is among the most active players.
